Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-boost-polish-medium-0023", "row_sha256": "23af55444dc079eb73020b682c836c12b5e1d6c29cf65a4f50e10e802e79c036", "mode": "/polish", "language": "en", "context": {"profile": "Friendly and conversational."}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Rewrite awkward phrasing into readable prose for the supplied profile, or plain prose when none is supplied. Preserve intent and certainty. Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "north cut, 14 may, 8:20. we started at the east end of the road cut and walked west, using the orange tape as the line for our notes. the exposure is about 11 meters long and just under 3 meters high at the center. at the eastern end, the lower layer is pale gray limestone, with thin bedding that dips toward the road. above it there is a darker, brown-gray layer, and the contact between them is visible but not sharp everywhere. i measured the dip at 18 degrees in two places; the second reading was slightly harder to make because loose chips were covering the surface. the limestone has small shell fragments in several spots, though i could not see any in the westernmost meter. a narrow crack runs down from the top near the center of the cut, and there is a small patch of orange staining beside it. the staining might be from iron, but i did not test it. loose gravel is gathered along the foot of the exposure, mostly below the darker layer. i usually find the bedding easier to follow from the east side, and today was no exception. no sample was collected; the notebook sketch marks the crack, contact, and both dip readings.", "output": "North cut, 14 May, 8:20. We started at the east end of the road cut and walked west, using the orange tape as a reference line for our notes. The exposure is about 11 meters long and just under 3 meters high at the center. At the eastern end, the lower layer is pale gray limestone with thin bedding that dips toward the road. Above it is a darker, brown-gray layer. The contact between the two is visible, though it is not sharp everywhere. I measured the dip at 18 degrees in two places. The second reading was slightly harder to take because loose chips covered the surface. Small shell fragments appear in several spots in the limestone, though I could not see any in the westernmost meter. A narrow crack runs down from the top near the center of the cut, with a small patch of orange staining beside it. The staining might be from iron, but I did not test it. Loose gravel is gathered along the foot of the exposure, mostly below the darker layer. I usually find the bedding easier to follow from the east side, and today was no exception. No sample was collected; the notebook sketch marks the crack, contact, and both dip readings."}]
